attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, written in his own voice.

semantics.note: A factual statement about the present: GPT-5 had not been released as of the post date. The 'exponential progress' wording is framing and is rightly left out of the score.

contract.note: The plain reading (no model named GPT-5 publicly released by 9 Jan 2025) is fair and ordinary. Leaving the rhetorical framing unscored is appropriate.

evidence.note: Dated 21 Dec 2024. Reports OpenAI had said Orion would not ship in 2024, so it was still unreleased shortly before the post.
Dated 21 Dec 2024 (summarising WSJ). Says GPT-5 was still in development and behind schedule.
OpenAI's own launch page dates GPT-5's introduction to 7 Aug 2025. This is a company disclosure that is consistent with no earlier release.

reviews.rationale: Reports from December 2024 show GPT-5 still in development and not released, and OpenAI's launch page dates the first release to August 2025. The packet has no sign of any release on or before 9 Jan 2025. The observation holds.

attribution.note: Marcus's own assertion in his own post.

semantics.note: 'Increasingly clear that they are struggling' is a firm statement about OpenAI's situation at the time, not a hedge. The normalised wording matches it.

contract.note: Reading 'struggling' as credible reports of delays, smaller-than-hoped gains or cost problems from late 2024 to the post date is an ordinary, fair reading. It is not stretched either way.

evidence.note: Dated 11 Nov 2024 (summarising The Information). OpenAI staff reported Orion's gains were far smaller than the GPT-3 to GPT-4 jump.
Dated 21 Dec 2024 (summarising WSJ). Reports slow training runs and results not yet worth the cost, while noting the model did beat its predecessors.

reviews.rationale: Two credible reports from within the period describe delays, smaller-than-hoped gains and cost problems in GPT-5/Orion development. Neither is confirmed by OpenAI, but both meet the support condition. Nothing in the packet shows the work on schedule or a GPT-5-worthy model shipped in the period.

attribution.note: Marcus explicitly stands by his own prediction.

semantics.note: 'We won't see AGI in 2025' is an unhedged forecast with a 2025 horizon. The hedged GPT-5 remark in the same sentence is correctly excluded.

contract.note: Reading it as 'no system widely accepted as AGI by 31 Dec 2025' is a fair, ordinary reading given that AGI has no agreed definition.

evidence.note: ARC Prize, 5 Dec 2025: the benchmark organisers say AGI is 'not yet' here.
ARC Prize, 5 Dec 2025: the ARC-AGI-2 grand prize went unclaimed in 2025.
Aug 2025 report quoting Altman: GPT-5 falls short of AGI as most people define it. This is a company statement, but it cuts against OpenAI's own interest.
Oct 2025 preprint scoring GPT-5 at 57% toward AGI. Marcus is a co-author, so it counts as context only.

reviews.rationale: The horizon ended on 31 Dec 2025. Benchmark organisers in December 2025 and OpenAI's CEO in August 2025 both said AGI had not been reached. The packet has no claim of AGI, widely accepted or not, during 2025. The short gap after 5 Dec does not change the result.
